subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Dynamic Application Security Testing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Dynamic Application Security Testing.

hook.text: SAST found nothing in the code. But the running application exposes an admin panel with no auth.

buildup.text: DAST tests the running application from the outside, probing it like an attacker would.

discovery.text: It finds runtime issues SAST can't: misconfigurations, exposed endpoints, and missing security headers.

twist.text: DAST can't see inside the code. It treats the app as a black box and reports what it finds exposed.

climax.text: Combining SAST and DAST covers both code-level and runtime vulnerabilities for comprehensive coverage.

punchline.text: SAST reads the code. DAST attacks the app. Use both.

quiz.question: How does DAST differ from SAST?
options: DAST tests the running application from outside
